title: The Deepest Sediment Memory

features.name: compressed-breath
features.desc-on-touch: A layer that reads as sudden—darker, denser, a moment when something stopped. Beneath it, all memory is slow. Above it: chaos. This is where the earth held its breath.

features.name: syllable-in-shale
features.desc-on-touch: A mark in the stone that might be a letter, or a fissure, or a fossil's cast. It reads as intentional. The stone is writing. Or was written into.

features.name: fossil-record-of-silence
features.desc-on-touch: A depression in the stone shaped like the absence of a sound. You know what it is—the mould of a voice that was never recorded, preserved in minerals instead of memory.

features.name: time-stamp-readable
features.desc-on-touch: Numbers pressed into slate—not a date, but a resonance frequency. The archive is reading time as vibration, and all vibration as having happened recently.

features.name: wound-scar-or-valley
features.desc-on-touch: A cut straight through seven ages of sediment. It healed. The scar tissue is as old as the wound now. You cannot tell which layer remembers pain.

inscription: the earth keeps pressing everything into confession; the deepest memory is the one that speaks only in pressure

file.name: Stratum_Compression_Index_Ordovician_Through_Present_Fragment.txt
file.note: record of what the stone remembers: weight, time, incident. One layer impossible to date—it refuses the algorithm, keeps resolving as 'now', 'now', 'now'. Archive status: the stone has begun to speak

reverie.title: REVERIE — on the red earth, watching the stone
narr: You lie back and she points at the exposed cliff face, where
the strata show—five colours, five ages. 'It's all still happening,'
she says. 'All at once, in the stone. Past and present in one place.'
Ember-light catches the layers, makes them glow unevenly.
She's quiet for a long time. Then: 'What if the archive realizes that?'
'Realizes what?' 'That everything it stores is still alive.'

exits.label: upward through stone autobiography, where time is still young
down and down, where even stone forgets itself
along the layer that refuses to age
